verdict: 20% cap at entry (S44984096): 15.9% / −24.2% against 17.0% / −28.4% for Sf5b94362. Without the cap, a very tight stop can make one position huge until the month-end trim (13 of 414 entries above 20% of equity; HINDALCO 2004 at 80%; ABB and SKF India in April 2016 at 36% and 34% on the same day). With the cap no entry exceeds 20%.

The cap costs almost nothing once luck is removed: in 200 random-pick runs its median is 16.4% (5th–95th 15.0–17.9%) against 16.3% (14.7–17.6%) uncapped, with the same median drawdown (−26.9% vs −27.3%). Sf5b94362's actual 17.0% was a lucky draw (79th percentile); the capped version's 15.9% an unlucky one (30th). The cap removes single-stock gap risk at no expected cost: recommended.

A (Sf5b94362), exit only when the weekly Supertrend turns bearish after entry: 17.0% CAGR / −28.4%, against 15.8% / −26.5% for S63387f09. +1.2 points a year for about 2 points more drawdown. Trades bought while the Supertrend was already bearish are now held until the stop, the 25-day time stop, or a later turn.

A is better in 3 of 5 windows (2000–04, 2005–09, 2020–26) and worse in 2010–14 and 2015–19. The gain is real but not uniform, and it is about the size of the random-pick spread for S63387f09 (14.1–16.7%).
A leans harder on a few big winners: the top 10 trades make 101% of net P&L (85% for S63387f09). Fewer trades (414 vs 530) because positions are held longer and slots fill.

B (Se5b28548), enter only while the weekly Supertrend is bullish: 14.9% / −29.6%. Worse on both counts. Waiting for confirmation enters later, with wider stops, and misses the early part of the recovery that the pullback setup is built to catch.
A + B (Sbb45ac25) is identical to B: if the Supertrend is bullish at entry, any later bearish week is a turn, so A changes nothing.
Recommendation: A is a reasonable upgrade if you accept slightly deeper drawdowns; it is not a clear-cut win. B should be rejected. The 2006 crash still sets the worst drawdown for all variants.
